title: The Night of the Murder
shared_passage:
Listen to a police officer interviewing Lucille Carrington about her husband's death. For questions 1 to 8, choose the correct answer.

DETECTIVE: You are Mrs Lucille Carrington?
Mrs CARRINGTON: Yes, that's right.
DETECTIVE: And your husband is – or, I should say, was – Mr James Carrington, who died two days ago at your home, 180 Portland Street.
Mrs CARRINGTON: Yes, James was my husband.
DETECTIVE: Doctors have carefully studied your husband's body. They have found that someone murdered your husband.
Mrs CARRINGTON: No! How?
DETECTIVE: A knife in his heart. We believe that he was sleeping at the time. He had taken sleeping pills.
Mrs CARRINGTON: I can't believe it!
DETECTIVE: It's true. So, Mrs Carrington, where were you on the day of his death, the fifth of June?
Mrs CARRINGTON: I was staying with a friend, in Stanhope. It's a village, about 50 miles from my home. My friend had been in hospital. I was looking after her. I was there from the 3rd of June until yesterday, when I heard the news.
DETECTIVE: Your friend's name is…?
Mrs CARRINGTON: Joanna Miller.
DETECTIVE: Joanna Miller. And on the afternoon of the 5th June – what were you doing?
Mrs CARRINGTON: I went into the city. Joanna was feeling tired and ill. I went to buy her some tea. Here, I have the receipts.
DETECTIVE: Did you go there alone?
Mrs CARRINGTON: Yes, I did. By car.
DETECTIVE: And did you also return to your house that afternoon?
Mrs CARRINGTON: No!
DETECTIVE: Your neighbour, Mrs Box, disagrees. She says that she saw you enter your house. You were wearing a long brown coat and a hat. She says she heard loud voices in the house. A man and a woman were arguing.
Mrs CARRINGTON: It wasn't me!
DETECTIVE: Oh? Then who was it?
Mrs CARRINGTON: I don't know… but, I believe that my husband had a lover. I think he was seeing another woman.
DETECTIVE: Who?
Mrs CARRINGTON: I don't know. But I have believed it for some time. I had smelled perfume on his clothes, and once I found a receipt for dinner for two people in his coat pocket. But James loves – loved me, I'm sure. Maybe she asked James to leave me and James refused, so she got angry and killed him.
DETECTIVE: Or maybe YOU got angry because he had a lover, and you killed him.
Mrs CARRINGTON: No!
DETECTIVE: We will find the truth.
